topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture topic and outlines the scope of the material to be covered.

topics.label: Recognition of Pathogens and Tissue Damage by Pattern Recognition Receptors
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the molecular mechanisms by which the innate immune system identifies infections and cellular damage using conserved molecular patterns and receptor signaling pathways.

topics.label: Sentinel Cell Activation, Leukocyte Recruitment, and Inflammatory Consequences
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how activated sentinel cells direct immune cell trafficking and migration to tissues and lymph nodes, as well as the systemic risks of excessive inflammatory activation.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammatory Responses
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how inflammation is brought to an end, how damaged tissues are repaired, and how persistent or unresolvable immune responses lead to chronic inflammatory structures.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture and announces the topic of the upcoming session.
